aaa_enabled.summary: Configure a TACACS+ or RADIUS server and name it in the authentication order, keeping local password as the fallback.
aaa_enabled.notes: Keep 'password' last in the authentication order so a server outage cannot lock every administrator out. 'commit confirmed' rolls the change back automatically if the session is lost.

secure_vty_transport.summary: Delete every cleartext service and keep SSH only.
cli: set system services ssh protocol-version v2
secure_vty_transport.notes: Confirm SSH reachability in a second session before the confirming commit: deleting telnet while SSH is unreachable strands the device.

vty_idle_timeout.summary: Apply an idle timeout on the login class used by administrative accounts.
cli: set system login class secure-ops idle-timeout 10
set system login class secure-ops permissions all
set system login user netops class secure-ops
vty_idle_timeout.notes: idle-timeout is expressed in minutes on the device; this tool normalizes it to seconds. A value of 0 means 'never' and is treated as a failure, not as an unconfigured value.

enable_secret_encrypted.summary: Set a root password (Junos prompts and stores it hashed) and pin the hash format.
cli: set system login password format sha512
# Junos prompts for the password and writes it back as encrypted-password
enable_secret_encrypted.notes: Junos hashes stored credentials by default and has no equivalent of 'service password-encryption', so this tool reports password_encryption as satisfied unless a plain-text-password statement is actually present in the configuration.

no_default_snmp_community.summary: Delete the default communities; prefer SNMPv3, or at minimum a non-default read-only string restricted by client prefix.
no_default_snmp_community.notes: The trailing 'clients 0.0.0.0/0 restrict' is what actually denies everything not explicitly permitted; without it the client list is advisory.

http_server_disabled.summary: Delete the HTTP listener; serve J-Web over HTTPS only, or remove web management entirely.
cli: set system services web-management https system-generated-certificate
set system services web-management https interface ge-0/0/1.0
http_server_disabled.notes: Bind HTTPS to an inside interface. A system-generated certificate protects the channel but not the identity of the device; use a CA-issued certificate where the management network warrants it.

ssh_version_2.summary: Pin the SSH protocol version explicitly rather than relying on the release default.
cli: set system services ssh protocol-version v2
set system services ssh root-login deny
ssh_version_2.notes: Releases from Junos 15.1 no longer accept v1 at all, but this tool will not infer the enforced version from a release string: with no protocol-version statement the control is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW rather than assumed compliant.

logging_enabled.summary: Send logs to a remote collector and keep a local file as a fallback.
cli: set system syslog host 10.20.30.40 any notice
set system syslog host 10.20.30.40 authorization info
set system syslog file messages any notice
set system syslog file interactive-commands interactive-commands any
logging_enabled.notes: 'interactive-commands' records the commands administrators actually ran, which is the log an incident review needs and the one most often missing.

management_acl.summary: Build a routing-engine protection filter and apply it inbound on lo0.0.
cli: set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term MGMT from source-address 10.20.30.0/24
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term MGMT from protocol tcp
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term MGMT from destination-port ssh
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term MGMT then accept
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term ESSENTIAL from protocol [ ospf vrrp icmp ]
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term ESSENTIAL then accept
set firewall family inet filter PROTECT-RE term DEFAULT then discard
set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet filter input PROTECT-RE
management_acl.notes: The final discard term drops everything not explicitly permitted, so enumerate what the device genuinely needs first - routing protocols, NTP, DNS, SNMP from the NMS, ICMP - or a commit will take the device off the network. 'commit confirmed 5' rolls back automatically if you lose the session, which is exactly the mistake this filter invites.

login_banner.summary: Set a pre-login message stating that access is restricted and activity is monitored.
cli: set system login message "Authorised access only. Activity is logged and monitored."
login_banner.notes: 'message' is shown before authentication and is the one this control looks for; 'announcement' is shown after and reaches only people who already got in. Do not name the device, its model or its software version - that is free reconnaissance.

password_min_length.summary: State the minimum length explicitly rather than relying on the release default.
cli: set system login password format sha512
set system login password change-type character-sets
password_min_length.notes: With no minimum-length statement this control reports NEEDS_REVIEW rather than FAIL: Junos does enforce a default, so the device is not unprotected, but the configuration text cannot say which default applies. Setting it explicitly is what makes the answer readable.

ntp_configured.summary: Point the device at two or more internal time sources.
ntp_configured.notes: Two sources let the device detect a lying one; a single source is a single point of failure for every timestamp it produces. Use 'set system ntp authentication-key' where the time source crosses an untrusted network.

no_write_snmp_community.summary: Remove every read-write community; use read-only with a client list, or SNMPv3 for write access.
no_write_snmp_community.notes: This is independent of the community's name: renaming a read-write community away from 'private' does not fix it. If write access is genuinely required, use SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy rather than a v2c community.
